extracted.intended_audience: aspiring romance authors, readers, editors, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and categorizing romance novels across market lines and subgenres, covering length, centrality of the romantic relationship, subgenre-specific constraints (time-travel, romantic suspense, inspirational, erotic, paranormal, etc.), trope usage, and handling of explicit content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance core requirement: relationship centrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The romantic relationship must be the central focus of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across subgenres the development of the protagonists' relationship should sit at the heart of the novel and drive plot and character decisions. For example, in romantic suspense the relationship 'must impact each decision they make and increase the tension of the suspense as it propel the story.' The relationship's trajectory (e.g., toward a solid relationship or an accepted 'happily ever after' / 'happily for now') is a primary measure of genre fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category romance: brevity and line-specific elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Category romances are short, mass-market lines where the author 'must pare the story down to its essentials. Subplots and minor characters are eliminated or relegated to the backstory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category lines each have a distinct identity—similar settings, characters, time periods, levels of sensuality, or types of conflict—and publishers usually issue guidelines for each line specifying elements necessary for inclusion. Writers should follow line-specific style/content/heat expectations and constrain scope to essentials; avoid complex subplot webs and many minor characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-title romance: length and publication expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-title novels are longer than category romances, typically between 350 and 400 pages, or 100,000–110,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-title work may be standalone or part of an interconnected series (not a category line). These novels remain on booksellers' shelves at store discretion. Authors and publishers may time releases for publicity; publishing cadence and wordcount expectations differ from category lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic suspense: interplay of mystery and relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Romantic suspense 'involves an intrigue or mystery for the protagonists to solve' while placing development of the relationship at the story's heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relationship must influence decisions and 'increase the tension of the suspense as it propel the story.' Conversely, the suspense events must directly affect the relationship and advance the plot. By the end the mystery is resolved and the relationship has evolved into a solid partnership. Language tends to be 'clean' (less explicit intimate description), and the novels are generally more plot-driven than character-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-travel romance: logical reactions and exploration of differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful time-travel romance 'must have the characters react logically to their experience and should investigate some of the differences, both physical and mental, between the world the character normally inhabits and the one where they landed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should responsibly portray characters' adjustment to differing eras (physical, cultural, mental differences). While some authors end with protagonists trapped in different periods (which can displease readers), the core requirement is believable character reaction and meaningful exploration of the temporal dislocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspirational/Christian romance constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspirational romance 'combines explicitly Christian themes with the development of a romantic relationship.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These novels typically avoid gratuitous violence or swearing; the central courtship is chaste and sex, if present, occurs after marriage and is not explicitly detailed. Many focus on the characters' faith (the love story as a triangle: man, woman, and their relationship with God) and commonly employ themes like forgiveness, honesty, and fidelity. Market placement (religious bookstores, specific lines) and audience expectations should guide content decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erotic romance: sexual content integrated with plot and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Erotic romance is 'characterized by strong sexual content' but remains distinct from pornography because it includes well-developed characters and a plot that could exist without the sex acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language is often straightforward rather than euphemistic; novels usually include more sex scenes and may focus more on the sex act. Crucially, sexual acts should progress the plot or further character development. Publishers and electronic presses differ in tolerance for explicit acts; taboo topics (pedophilia, incest, bestiality) are discouraged by publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paranormal romance: blend of real and fantastic; worldbuilding spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Paranormal romance 'blends the real with the fantastic or science fictional' (vampires, werewolves, witches, ghosts, time travel, extraterrestrials, psychic abilities, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These novels vary in how much they develop alternate realities: some keep attention strongly on the underlying romance and downplay world specifics, while others 'develop the alternate reality meticulously, combining well-planned magical systems and inhuman cultures with contemporary reality.' Authors should choose the level of worldbuilding appropriate to their story and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science fiction & fantasy romance: balance worldbuilding with romance
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction romance and fantasy/romantic fantasy blend speculative world elements with a fully developed romance; sensuality levels can vary from chaste to explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While exploring alternate worlds (futuristic settings, other planets, steampunk alternate history), these books must still deliver a fully developed romantic plot. Publishers have sometimes included such works in contemporary series lines; authors should ensure the speculative elements support rather than overshadow the central relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tropes: reader-expected plot devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Tropes are common themes or plot devices repeatedly used in romance novels that readers seek out (examples: Love triangle; Friends to Lovers; Forced Proximity; Enemies to Lovers; Forbidden Love; Second Chance; Fake Relationship; Soulmates; Arranged Marriage; Workplace romances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tropes connect to readers via 'universal experiences and archetypes' and can be a reliable way to attract an audience. Writers may innovate from or intentionally subvert tropes for effect. Distinguish tropes (plot devices) from 'hooks' (character or setting elements like profession or location) when designing a manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit content handling and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit content ('spice,' 'steam,' 'heat') is subjective and involves not just amount but type and level of sexual description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some publishers or authors list content ratings for their books based on their own guidelines; library catalog labeling of explicit content is controversial (ALA views labeling as a form of censorship). Libraries may use tags to aid staff. Authors/publishers should be aware of audience expectations, market norms, and potential controversy when labeling or rating explicit material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher/market formatting and line guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers and market formats influence what kinds of romances are published (e.g., mass‑market vs trade vs hardcover, series/lines vs single‑title) and publish line-specific submission/guideline documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical mass-market romances are less often published in hardcover; publishers begin/terminate lines based on market preferences (e.g., erotic or Christian lines introduced, Regency lines ended). Authors targeting particular markets should follow publisher-issued line guidelines (elements, heat level, settings, timing) and recognize that format affects distribution and shelving.
